issue.masthead: no. 157 · North Hollow · sunrise 07:18 · waxing crescent

pieces.title: On winter squash skin
pieces.body: "If you cannot dent the squash rind with your thumbnail after a full afternoon in the sun, it will keep on the cellar rack until March without rotting. If your thumbnail leaves a mark, bake it with butter before Sunday."

pieces.title: Parlour window sash eased and refitted
pieces.body: The sticking lower sash on the parlour west window moves freely on its tracks after half an hour with the block plane and a rub of paraffin wax. Silas planed three light shavings off the bottom rail and wiped the pulley channels clean of grit. The counterweight now holds the sash open at any height without wedging a pine stick underneath.

pieces.title: Glass carboys return from summer storage
pieces.body: Six five-gallon glass carboys arrived back in the mudroom after spending the summer stacked on dry straw in the outbuilding. Each jug was inspected for hairline checks, soaked in lukewarm washing soda, and rinsed twice with clear well water. They now stand upside down on clean flour sacks in the cellar alcove, waiting for the weekend press run.

pieces.title: Goldenrod fades along the lower stone wall
pieces.body: The wild goldenrod along the orchard perimeter has begun turning to pale down, signaling the closing days of warm afternoons. Heavy bumblebees were working the last yellow florets at midday, moving slowly in the fifty-degree shade. Nora gathered three dried bundles for the mantle, leaving the remaining stalks untouched for small winter seed birds.
pieces.reason: seasonal observation recorded in garden notes

pieces.title: on the east sill
pieces.body: the sun touched the kitchen counter at seven fourteen this morning, which is six minutes later than last week. the wood stove is cold and the copper kettle has not boiled yet. two field mice were seen near the compost bin. they looked busy and polite. the inbox has four envelopes in it. none of them appear urgent.
